name: Philip Meyer
life: “I still remember pronouncing two surnames over the noise of a wedding trolley.” People around the brick passage off the shop row know Philip by a small Tuesday habit. Philip takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I offered to officiate because I could do the ceremony in both their languages. I had forgotten my own wedding anniversary.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. Philip has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, with black hair twisted into a small knot. Philip takes off the watch before a long conversation during a conversation.
personality: Philip takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Philip can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To give both languages equal space in the vows.
family: Percy Davila is Philip’s half-sibling. Philip chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Percy brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The free fringe*, Percy says, “I used the free offer as an excuse to get out of my room after my husband left.”
connections: Lucia Ferreira. A bilingual ceremony and a fog-bound photograph leave the vows at the center of the afternoon.

reactions.situation: Fog hides the sea during the vows
reactions.response: Philip asks the couple if they want to begin under fog or wait, without extending the celebration for a photograph.
